observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard, all close in size. South shows a stooped, spindly biped from the front, facing the camera: a scowling face with a large grey-blue hooked beak, pink lips and small yellow eyes under a heavy brow. It has two very large thin pink-veined ears that sweep out and curl at the tips, a ginger mane over the head and shoulders, a bare wrinkled tan-pink pot belly, long thin arms with long clawed fingers, bird-like clawed feet, and a long thin tail curling off to the viewer's left. East is a true right-facing side profile of the same animal: the beak points right, the ears sweep back, the back is hunched, the belly is round, the legs are spindly and clawed, and the tail curls behind. North shows the back: the ears seen from behind, the back of a hairy head, a shaggy ruff over the shoulders, a bare wrinkled back and haunches, and the tail curling off to the viewer's right. There is no face on north.
observed.south.png: The front view at full resolution. The face looks at the camera: a glossy slate blue-grey hooked beak, which is the darkest element of the face, pink fleshy lips, small yellow eyes and a frowning brow. The skin is wrinkled tan-pink and the belly is a bare pot belly. The crown and shoulder hair is ginger and fairly dense. The fingers are long with curved claws, and the toes are long and bird-like with claws. The rendering is painterly and realistic, with a clean cut-out.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The beak is a hooked parrot-like beak with pink lips, the eye is yellow, and ginger hair runs from the crown to a shaggy shoulder ruff. Both ears sweep back to curled points. The belly protrudes, the posture is stooped, and the arms and legs are spindly with long clawed digits. The tail is long and curls behind. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear view. Both ears are seen from behind, the back of the head is covered in ginger hair, and the shaggy ruff runs down the upper back. The lower back, buttocks and legs are bare and wrinkled, and the tail comes from the base of the spine and curls to the viewer's right. There are no eyes or face. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands about as tall as the vanilla human sprite, a little taller with the ears. At 32 px per cell it reads as an orange-and-pink spindly figure with wide ears and a curled tail, clearly separate from the ground and bigger than the rat. Zoomed out it becomes a small orange blob.

reply.subject: RM_Venomvine

observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A flat, low mat of thin rust-red to maroon woody runners. They spread out from a central knot in a rough star, crossing one another. Every runner carries many small pale, hooked thorns along its length. Dark olive-green, serrated, holly-like leaves with rust edges are scattered along the runners, thickest in the centre. The mat is seen at the game's angle, wider than it is tall, and fills most of the canvas width. The background is transparent checkerboard: no soil, shadow or ground patch. The rendering is painterly and fairly realistic, with a dark edge on the runners.

At max zoom, the mat covers about one cell, a little wider than the human's body, and lies flat on the ground. It is clearly a ground cover: a tangle of thorny red-brown runners with dark leaves. At 32 px/cell it shrinks to a faint brown scribble that is low-contrast against the soil and reads as dry twigs or debris. In the ×4 nearest view it is a brown, twiggy star, and the leaves are barely visible. Zoomed out at 18 px/cell it is a small dark smudge.

SIGNATURE.seen: The rust-dark runners and the many recurved hooked thorns along them are clearly visible. The venom is not drawable, and the thorns sit on top of the runners rather than only beneath, which is acceptable from the game camera.

READS_KIND.seen: A low, flat, spreading mat of runners; it reads as ground cover, not a lump.

NATURAL.seen: The runners branch irregularly and the leaves vary; it looks grown. The radial star layout is slightly regular, but it is not man-made.

ANCHOR.seen: A flat mat lying in the cell with nothing cut off. As ground cover it has no trunk to anchor.

NO_SCENERY.seen: Clean alpha with no soil disc, shadow or rocks.

ALIEN.seen: The rust-maroon runners and dark serrated leaves resemble bramble canes but are not a plain Earth species. The rust palette and dense hooked thorns give it an off-world look, though it is close to a blackberry runner.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic shading on the stems and leaves; not cel-shaded or cartoon.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the description (rust runners, recurved thorns); not a vanilla plant texture.

FILLS.seen: The mat spans almost the full canvas width and about 160 px of height, which suits a flat mat at the game's camera angle.

SCALE.seen: About one cell and ankle-low beside the human, which fits a low mat that catches ankles.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the thin runners become a faint brown scribble, low-contrast against the soil, and the leaves vanish.

VARIANTS.seen: No variants.png was given. The provenance says 'growth variant c', which suggests a pool exists, but I cannot see its other members.

edits.change: The runners are segmented like jointed chitin: each runner is a chain of short, swollen, rust-dark nodes with a pale seam at every joint, creeping flat across the ground instead of arching like woody canes.
Beneath the runners, venom hooks grow in matched pairs at each joint, two glossy recurved claws curling toward each other like pincers, with a bead of sickly green-amber venom at each tip.

request.prompt: A single RimWorld ground-cover plant sprite, the venomvine: a low, flat mat of rust-dark creeping runners rooted in the best shade, spreading to fill about 1.2 cells. Each runner is segmented like jointed chitin: a chain of short, swollen, rust-dark nodes with a pale seam at every joint, lying close to the ground in sinuous, interlocking curves. At every node a single asymmetric fused leaf blade grows out, a lopsided fan of rust and deep-maroon tissue with smooth edges and parallel ribs, one side much longer than the other, so the foliage reads as flat, uneven, unfamiliar shapes. Beneath and between the runners, venom hooks grow in matched pairs at each joint: two glossy, dark recurved claws curling toward each other like pincers, each tip carrying a small bead of sickly green-amber venom, visible where the runners lift slightly off the ground. Palette: deep rust, dark brown-red and maroon, with pale seams and small venom-green accents. Viewed from above at a slight three-quarter angle, the mat centred in the frame. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic rendering, clean dark outline, no ground plate.
